title: Perf suite: add mixed prompt-length + mixed streaming scenarios for SLO-tier batching
creator: Marcus Reed
description:
Context
- Tiered batching defaults (fast/standard/cost-efficient) are expected to behave well under realistic traffic: mixed prompt lengths, mixed streaming vs non-streaming, and bursty concurrency.
- Our current perf suite scenarios over-index on single workload shapes (e.g., uniform prompt length, all streaming or all non-streaming). This missed a fast-tier p99 regression in earlier canary where long-prefill requests dominated queue head-of-line behavior.

Goal
Extend benchmark-lab/perf suite with mixed scenarios that better approximate production traffic and catch scheduler regressions before canary/rollout.

Deliverable
- New perf suite scenarios that combine:
  1) prompt-length mixture (short/medium/long) and
  2) request type mixture (streaming + non-streaming)
  3) concurrency ramps (steady-state + step + burst)
- Each scenario must emit tier-labelled metrics and produce pass/fail outputs consumable by perf-canary gating.

References
- Confluence: batching SLO tier benchmark methodology: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/batching-slo-tier-benchmark-methodology.json
- Perf canary gating ticket: ENG-18428
- Workload signal features: ENG-18423
- Upstream work landed as benchmark-lab PR: sources/github/benchmark-lab/pr-612-add-mixed-workload-slo-tier-scenarios.json

Scenario design (v1)
1) Mixed lengths + mixed streaming ("MIXED_A")
- Distribution (prompt tokens):
  - 60% short: 32–256
  - 30% medium: 256–1,024
  - 10% long: 1,024–4,096
- Output tokens:
  - short: 64–256
  - medium: 128–512
  - long: 256–1,024
- Streaming ratio: 70% streaming / 30% non-streaming
- Concurrency profile:
  - warm-up 5m @ 30% target RPS
  - steady 10m @ target RPS
  - burst 2m @ 1.5x target RPS
  - cool-down 3m

2) Long-prefill interference ("MIXED_B")
- Distribution (prompt tokens):
  - 80% short: 32–256
  - 20% very long: 2,048–8,192 (prefill-heavy)
- Streaming ratio: 50/50
- Purpose: ensure fast tier tail latency protection and anti-starvation behavior doesn’t regress when long-prefill requests arrive during steady decode load.

3) Streaming-heavy interactive ("MIXED_C")
- Prompt lengths skew short/medium; 90% streaming.
- Purpose: validate chunk cadence/first-token latency and ensure batching doesn’t cause visible jitter.

Workload realism notes
- Token distributions based on aggregated Hosted API telemetry buckets (no tenant-specific data), aligned with the methodology doc.
- We intentionally include a long-prefill minority to surface head-of-line blocking and backpressure behavior.

Implementation plan
- Add scenario configs to benchmark-lab:
  - New YAML/JSON scenario definitions for MIXED_A/B/C
  - Load generator updates to support per-request streaming flag and token-length sampling from a mixture distribution
  - Ensure each request includes tier selection so we can run the same scenario across fast/standard/cost-efficient.
- Metrics & outputs:
  - Emit latency percentiles separately for:
    - TTFT (time-to-first-token) for streaming
    - end-to-end latency for non-streaming
    - per-token decode latency (where supported)
  - Record batch size distribution and queue depth (if available) as diagnostic artifacts.
  - Produce a machine-readable summary (JSON) consumed by perf-canary baseline comparison.
- Gate integration (owned by ENG-18428 but validated here):
  - Confirm scenario outputs contain tier dimension and stable metric names.

Acceptance criteria
- MIXED_A/B/C scenarios run successfully in benchmark-lab CI on at least the top 2 model families used for tier validation.
- Scenarios are reproducible across 3 consecutive runs with <5% variance in p95 under stable conditions (document variance envelope; we don’t need perfect determinism).
- Perf-canary can consume scenario outputs and enforce tier-specific pass/fail thresholds without manual parsing.
- Scenario artifacts include enough diagnostics to triage failures (at minimum: per-phase RPS, concurrency, batch size histogram, queue depth series).

Out of scope (v1)
- Full replay of production traces.
- Tenant-specific distributions.
- Multi-region routing behaviors.

Risks / mitigations
- High test flakiness due to GPU contention / noisy neighbors
  - Mitigation: add longer steady windows, define acceptable variance envelope, and pin dedicated benchmark runners.
- Metric cardinality explosion when adding dimensions
  - Mitigation: only tag scenario_id, tier, model_family, hardware_class; no per-request IDs.

Rollout
- Land in benchmark-lab behind a flag "mixed_workload_scenarios_v1".
- Enable on nightly perf runs first.
- Promote to pre-merge perf canary gating once variance is characterized and baseline established.

Definition of Done
- Code merged in benchmark-lab
- Scenario docs added to perf suite README
- Baselines captured and linked in ENG-18428

Links
- Merged: sources/github/benchmark-lab/pr-612-add-mixed-workload-slo-tier-scenarios.json

2026-03-11 — Sofia Ivanova: For MIXED_B, add a starvation check: verify short streaming requests maintain TTFT under long-prefill arrivals. (Resolved: added TTFT threshold reporting for the short cohort.)
